catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds the output-off/safe-state action of a programmable DC source with device_kind instrument. cap.motion.stop.v1 lists only robot.arm, robot.mobile_base and motion.axis, and cap.device.configure.v1 has minProperties 1, so neither can be the no-input safe-state action required at R2. The extension takes no input and writes OUTP OFF.

notes:
DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the family-config ScpiDriver helper is replaced by a direct Driver over comm.bridge:EAPowerSupply with native.py. The upstream interface is a Python object whose methods issue the SCPI commands and cache the V/I setpoints locally (comm/bridge.py:132-143, comm/bridge.py:299-305); a command table would bypass the native object and its cache. The wire commands are still the upstream's own (VOLT, CURR, OUTP, the MEAS queries through read_meas_fast, OUTP:STAT? and SYST:ERR?). What is covered: measured voltage, current and power; cached voltage and current setpoints; output state; SCPI error code; writes for the voltage setpoint, current setpoint and output relay; the @estop and the safe-state action both write OUTP OFF. R2 is declared because the source delivers 5 kW into the DUT; the independent stop is the x-cap.laristizabal1.output_off.v1 safe-state action because the clone has no vendor-text hardware e-stop. NOT COVERED: no power setpoint is exposed (the native EAPowerSupply has no power command; SCPIController.set_power_fast belongs to another upstream class and is not reachable through this native); no run_profile action (run_profile is on SCPIController, not EAPowerSupply); the DL3000 electronic load (comm/dl3000.py) is not exposed because this package models the source, and the load is a separate USB-TMC instrument. The measured fields come from the upstream MEAS reads; the setpoint fields come from the upstream local cache, not a device readback (the clone never queries the setpoints). The fake's initial values and replies are test data marked '# placeholder'; its measured values follow the cached setpoints only while the output is on. The gate ran the fake backend only: no hardware was attached, no hardware run was made, and no human reviewed or tested the package. reviewed_by is null and the package is model-authored. The last gate run passed G1-G9 with no warnings (evidence contract_checked; never an MHS-Device level).
